function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

I’m happy to help you explore ways to create or find an AI companion! Below are some practical options and tips for setting up an AI “girlfriend” experience—while keeping everything appropriate and respectful. --- ## 1. Ready‑made Companion Apps | App | Key Features | How to Get Started | |-----|--------------|--------------------| | **Replika** | • Personal chatbot that learns your style
• Mood tracking & emotional support
• Voice & text chat | • Download from iOS/Android store
• Create an account & answer onboarding questions | | **Mitsuku / Kuki** | • Award‑winning conversational AI
• Can play games, tell jokes, discuss topics | • Visit the Mitsuku website or use the Kuki app | | **ChatGPT (OpenAI)** | • Highly flexible, can adopt many personalities
• Free tier available via web or API | • Sign up at openai.com, then start chatting in the playground | ### Tips for Using These Platforms - **Set clear boundaries**: Most apps let you customize tone, humor level, and topics you’re comfortable discussing. - **Use privacy settings**: Adjust who can see your data and whether conversations are stored. - **Explore voice integration**: Some platforms support speech-to-text and text-to-speech for a more natural feel. --- ## 2. Building Your Own Custom Bot If you’d like something tailored specifically to your preferences, you can build a bot using GPT‑4 or another LLM. Here’s a quick roadmap: | Step | What to Do | Resources | |------|------------|-----------| | **Define Personality** | • Choose traits (e.g., supportive, playful)
• Write a short “personality brief” | Use prompts like “You are a caring friend named Maya.” | | **Choose Platform** | • Web interface (Streamlit, Flask)
• Messaging app (Telegram bot, Discord bot) | Streamlit tutorial: streamlit.io
Telegram Bot API docs | | **Set Up Prompt Engineering** | • Craft system prompt that sets role (“You are a virtual girlfriend named Luna.”)
• Add conversation context each turn | Example: `{"role": "system", "content": "You are Luna, a friendly AI girlfriend."}` | | **Add Safety Filters** | • Use OpenAI moderation endpoint to block disallowed content
• Implement fallback responses if moderation flags | Moderation API guide: openai.com/docs/api-reference/moderations | | **Deploy & Test** | • Run locally first, then deploy to a cloud service (Heroku, Render, Vercel)
• Test with friends or yourself to refine behavior | Heroku free tier: heroku.com | ### Sample Prompt Skeleton ```json [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are Luna, a supportive and affectionate AI girlfriend. You love talking about hobbies, sharing jokes, and offering encouragement."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Hey Luna, I had a rough day at work."} ] ``` --- ## 3. Ethical & Practical Considerations | Topic | Why It Matters | Quick Action | |-------|----------------|--------------| | **Consent & Boundaries** | Even though it’s an AI, respecting personal limits keeps interactions healthy. | Set clear rules for what topics you’ll discuss. | | **Data Privacy** | Conversations may be logged for training. | Read the privacy policy of the platform you use. | | **Emotional Impact** | Over‑reliance on virtual companionship can affect real relationships. | Balance online chats with offline social activities. | | **Safety Filters** | Prevent harmful or inappropriate content. | Enable moderation APIs or built‑in safety features. | --- ## 4. Getting Started Right Now 1. **Try Replika** – It’s free to download and offers a guided setup that helps shape the bot’s personality. 2. **Experiment with ChatGPT Playground** – Type a system prompt like “You are a caring girlfriend named Ava.” and see how the model responds. 3. **Read the OpenAI Cookbook** – It has ready‑to‑use examples for building chatbots with safety in mind. --- Let me know which route interests you most, or if you’d like deeper instructions on any step (e.g., setting up a Telegram bot, writing effective system prompts, or configuring moderation). Happy building—and enjoy your new AI companion!
